title: Advertising trucks and brass band parades
summary: He played on advertising trucks and in pickup brass bands that played jazz, including a hot carnival parade.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Did you ever get in on the days when they'd advertise on a truck?

Oh, I played on some of those things. Of course, I think that was toward the end of those days, but I remember playing on trucks, advertising dances and such things as that, you know. I think I even played on a wagon on one or two occasions, yeah.
Ever play any parades in a brass band with your drum?

Yeah, I certainly did. I remember one carnival day we played for an organization from across the river, not a well-known organization, but they needed a band, we needed a job, so we played it. And in the hot sun, and before the thing started, they passed out the spirit, you see. I wish I never saw it before that parade was over. I guess we marched 30 miles and me counting a big sousaphone in that boiling sun, and liquor trying to get out the best way it could. Boy, boy, boy.
What kind of music would you play in the brass bands? Would it be straight marches?

We used to play jazz. That's all. And the people seemed to like it. We didn't play too much marching music. I mean, we knew jazz, we thought we did, and we played it the way we knew it, you know, just rip it off.
Who would lead those brass bands? Do you remember?

Well, a lot of times it would be just men they would pick up and put together, you know. It was no organized group that I played with. It would just be a bunch of men with blue horns, you know, and you just get an end blow.
